attachments.insertion_landmark: proximal phalanx of the great toe, base, medial side (via the medial sesamoid)

actions: abducts and flexes the great toe, supports the medial longitudinal arch

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Most medial and superficial of the first (superficial) layer of plantar intrinsic muscles; forms the medial border of the foot, palpable along the medial arch.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Three described sites within the muscle belly along the medial border of the foot, corresponding to the region of highest medial plantar nerve branch density (the same quadrant in which the trigger points are described).
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain along the medial border of the foot and the medial heel, in a distribution that overlaps clinically with plantar fasciitis-type medial heel pain.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Prolonged standing/walking on a pronated or flat foot, ill-fitting or unsupportive footwear, and overuse from repetitive hallux abduction/flexion.
trigger_points.notes: A common contributor to, and mimic of, medial plantar heel pain/plantar fasciitis; abductor hallucis trigger points were also documented among active myofascial trigger points reproducing symptoms in patients with plantar heel pain.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2 (Lower Extremities), 1999 -- as cited in secondary summaries (e.g. Morningside Acupuncture NYC 'Abductor Hallucis Trigger Points') describing the medial-foot/medial-heel referral pattern; trigger-point site correlates with the medial plantar nerve entry quadrant per Wada JT, Akamatsu F, Hojaij F, Itezerote A, Scarpa JC, Andrade M, Jacomo A (2020) 'An Anatomical Basis for the Myofascial Trigger Points of the Abductor Hallucis Muscle.' Biomed Res Int 2020:9240581, doi:10.1155/2020/9240581 -- retrieved via PubMed
